lede: A lens is a piece of glass with curved faces, and every ray that crosses it is refracted twice. One shape brings light together; the other spreads it apart. Which one you have, and how strongly it bends light, is the whole of this topic.
can: Tell a converging lens from a diverging one, by shape and by symbol
Define focal length using the principal focus and the centre of the lens
Measure a focal length with a distant object, a screen and a metre rule

md: Hold a magnifying glass up to a window on a sunny day and you can burn a bright dot onto a sheet of paper. Hold up the lens from a pair of short-sighted glasses and the light spreads out instead. The difference is the shape of the glass.

md:
A **converging** lens (also called convex) is **fat in the middle**. A **diverging** lens (concave) is **thin in the middle**.
In a ray diagram you never draw the curved glass. You draw a straight vertical line with arrowheads: **outwards** for converging, **inwards** for diverging. The arrowheads are the only thing that tells the two apart on paper.

prompt: In the figure above, which lens is the converging one?
options: the one that is fat in the middle
the one that is thin in the middle
answer: the one that is fat in the middle
explain: Fat in the middle converges. It is worth saying the two words together every time, because swapping them is the commonest slip on this topic.

md:
Send in rays that are **parallel to the principal axis** and a converging lens brings them all to one point. That point is the **principal focus**, written **F**.
The distance between the **centre of the lens** and the principal focus is the **focal length**. A fatter lens bends light more, so its focal length is shorter.

title: Why parallel rays, and not any old rays?
md: Because only parallel rays all meet at the same point. Rays from a nearby object arrive spread out and meet somewhere else, further from the lens — which is why the focal length is defined for parallel rays, and why the practical uses a distant object.

prompt: Rays arriving parallel to the principal axis of a converging lens all pass through one point on the axis. What is that point called? (two words)
answer: principal focus | the principal focus | principal focal point
explain: The principal focus, marked F on every diagram. CCEA examiners have reported candidates not knowing where to label it.

md:
A diverging lens spreads parallel rays apart. They never meet, so its principal focus is found by tracing the spreading rays **backwards** until the dashed lines cross, on the **same side as the light came from**.
CCEA asks you to tell the two lenses apart, and to define the focal length for a **converging** lens. Ray diagrams for diverging lenses are not on this specification.

title: What examiners have written about the two lenses
md: **Summer 2024 Foundation Q2:** a significant minority got converging and diverging **the wrong way round**. **Summer 2023 Foundation Q8** and **Higher Q3** found the opposite — most candidates did recognise a concave, diverging lens, so the naming itself is learnable.

prompt: A lens is thin in the middle and thick at its edges. What happens to rays that arrive parallel to its principal axis?
options: they spread apart, as though coming from a point on the near side
they meet at a point on the far side
they carry straight on without bending
answer: they spread apart, as though coming from a point on the near side
explain: Thin in the middle diverges. The rays spread, and the point they seem to come from is on the same side as the incoming light.

text: 4. The four things every lens diagram needs

alt: A converging lens symbol standing on a horizontal principal axis, with the optical centre at the middle of the lens, the principal focus marked with a cross on each side and the focal length marked from the lens to the focus.

caption: Axis, centre, focus on both sides, focal length. Draw these before any ray.

md:
The **principal axis** is the horizontal line through the middle of the lens. The **optical centre** is the point where it crosses the lens. **F** is marked on **both** sides, the same distance out each way.
So the definition you write is: the focal length is the distance between the **centre of the lens** and the **principal focus**.

prompt: Complete the definition. A converging lens's focal length is the distance from the principal focus to the __ of the lens. (two words)
answer: optical centre | centre | the optical centre
explain: The optical centre. A Unit 7 Booklet B question gave a mark for these two words, and candidates could not recall them.

md:
**Question.** Three measurements of lens-to-screen distance are 14.8 cm, 15.1 cm, 14.9 cm, and a fourth reading of 19.4 cm. Find the focal length.
**Step 1** — spot the odd one out: 19.4 cm is far from the other three, so it is anomalous and is left out.
**Step 2** — add the three that agree and divide by three.
**Answer** — the focal length is 14.9 cm.

prompt: A student's lens-to-screen readings are 9.4 cm, 9.6 cm, 9.5 cm and 13.1 cm. Ignoring the anomalous reading, what is the focal length in cm, to one decimal place?
explain: 13.1 cm is the anomaly, so leave it out: (9.4 + 9.6 + 9.5) ÷ 3 = 9.5 cm. Including an anomalous result in a mean has cost marks in Booklet B twice.

title: Convex Lenses
why: Four minutes on what a converging lens does to parallel rays, and where the principal focus is.

title: Two things in this video that CCEA does not ask for
md: Lenses sit in the separate-Physics specifications on the other boards, so videos for this topic are labelled Triple and carry extra material. Two parts go beyond CCEA Double Award: **ray diagrams for diverging (concave) lenses**, and **magnification = image height ÷ object height** as a calculation. Watch them if you like; neither is examined here.

prompt: Which of these does CCEA Double Award Science ask you to do with a diverging lens?
options: recognise it and say that it spreads parallel rays apart
draw a full ray diagram to find the image it forms
calculate the magnification of the image it forms
answer: recognise it and say that it spreads parallel rays apart
explain: Recognise it, and describe what it does. Ray diagrams for diverging lenses and the magnification equation belong to the separate-Physics specifications.

task: Drag the focal-length slider from its smallest value to its largest and watch the two F marks move. Notice which setting makes the lens fattest, and check that a fatter lens always has the shorter focal length.

prompt: In the simulation you make the converging lens fatter in the middle. What happens to its focal length?
explain: Shorter. A fatter lens refracts each ray through a bigger angle, so the rays meet closer to the lens.

md:
Name a lens as converging or diverging from its shape and from its symbol.
Say what each lens does to rays arriving parallel to the principal axis.
Define the focal length as the distance from the optical centre to the principal focus.
Describe the distant-object method and take a mean that leaves an anomaly out.

This usually opens with a picture of a lens or its symbol and one mark for naming it, then the definition of focal length, then three marks for the method: a **distant object**, a **screen** moved until the image is sharp, and the **lens-to-screen distance** measured. If you are stuck on the definition, name the two points it runs between. If a set of readings has an odd one out, leave it out of the mean and say why.
